perso.name: Personalization (1:1)
perso.gloss: Tailoring the message to the individual, not the segment.

genai.gloss: Models that produce content — copy, images, replies — from a prompt.

agentic.gloss: Systems that don't just generate, they decide and act toward a goal.

decis.name: Agentic decisioning
decis.gloss: An agent choosing what to say, when, how often and on which channel — per person.

bandit.name: Bandits / RL
bandit.gloss: The maths that lets a system learn which choice wins by trying and measuring.

cep.name: CEP
cep.gloss: Customer Engagement Platform — where this messaging actually runs.

geo.name: GEO

govern.name: Governance
govern.gloss: The controls that make automated decisions safe, explainable and legible.

stories.head: AI budgets are growing faster than proof of ROI
stories.plain: Marketing teams are pouring money into AI — especially agentic projects — but most deployments haven't reached full scale and few can show a clear financial return. This matters because budget holders will eventually demand proof, and the gap between spend and demonstrated value is where programmes get cut or restructured.

stories.head: Not everyone in marketing should be an AI builder
stories.plain: Marketing orgs are over-indexing on people who build AI tools and ignoring the maintainers, monitors, and everyday users those tools need to stay safe and effective. Governance roles — the people who watch what AI does day-to-day — are being left unfilled, which is a structural risk as automation scales.

stories.head: Fibr AI CEO on making your website legible to AI agents, not just humans
stories.plain: Fibr AI's CEO argues that AI agents are now a second audience for every website, and being cited accurately by those agents matters more than just showing up. This is a practical GEO conversation — how brands structure content so AI systems cite them correctly when answering customer queries.

stories.head: Validity Engage adds MCP connector to bring email intelligence into AI tools
stories.plain: Validity's email platform now ships a Model Context Protocol connector, letting AI assistants pull pre-send deliverability and engagement data without switching tools. MCP is becoming a de-facto plumbing standard for agentic marketing stacks, so this signals how established MarTech vendors are repositioning to stay relevant inside AI workflows.

stories.head: Morrisons grows loyalty-linked sales from 47% to 65% in 18 months using Eagle Eye AIR
stories.plain: UK supermarket Morrisons used Eagle Eye's AI platform to rebuild its loyalty programme and lifted the share of sales tied to loyalty cards by 18 percentage points in 18 months. It's a rare quantified retail AI ROI case study, making it useful evidence for teams trying to justify similar investment.

stories.head: AI budgets are growing faster than proof of ROI
stories.plain: Most marketing AI projects are still not at full scale, yet budgets keep rising. The core problem: teams can't show clear financial value for what they're spending. This shapes how AI is bought — and whether finance teams will keep approving the spend. A must-read for anyone pitching or defending AI investment.

stories.head: Tealium calls Jev AI decision model for real-time next-best-action after cart abandonment
stories.plain: Tealium's CDP triggers a lightweight AI decision model — Jev — to pick the next best action after a cart abandonment, without routing every call through an expensive LLM. This is a concrete, working example of agentic decisioning inside a live CEP stack, showing how cost and latency can be managed in real deployments.

stories.head: OpenAI adds visual ad formats to ChatGPT with new measurement tools
stories.plain: ChatGPT is rolling out richer visual ad formats alongside measurement capabilities — but bot traffic is already inflating click numbers. This matters because a new ad channel inside an AI answer engine changes both media buying and how brands think about visibility in AI-generated responses. Fraud risk is already present at launch.

stories.head: Agentic media buying needs malware guardrails built into optimization logic
stories.plain: As AI agents take over more campaign decisions autonomously, traffic-quality and security signals must become part of what those agents optimize for — not an afterthought. This piece raises a governance gap specific to agentic buying: agents optimizing on bad signals can scale fraud faster than humans ever did.

stories.head: Fibr AI CEO: AI agents are your website's second audience — being cited correctly matters more than being cited
stories.plain: Ankur Goyal argues that AI agents now read and act on your website independently of human visitors, making accurate brand representation inside AI-generated answers a new priority. Getting cited is not enough — the citation must be correct. This reframes GEO from an SEO add-on into a brand safety issue.

month.skicker: 30-day synthesis · the shape underneath the feed

themes.head: AI Budgets Outrun Proof of Value
body: Spending on AI tools is accelerating across marketing organisations, but measurement frameworks have not kept pace. Executives are approving larger budgets while finance teams struggle to attribute outcomes, creating a dangerous credibility gap that risks a backlash when results disappoint.

The pressure is sharpened by findings that a significant slice of AI cost goes to automating routine, rules-based work — the lowest-value use case. Marketers who cannot articulate what incremental lift AI delivers will face hard questions in the next budget cycle, making ROI literacy the skill that matters most right now.
ev: Pega CFO on what's inside AI budgets
MarTech · Get more without spending more

themes.head: Agentic Automation Replaces Classic Workflows
body: The rule-based, campaign-centric model of marketing automation is being declared obsolete as AI agents capable of autonomous decision-making move into production. The shift is not incremental — agents handle sequencing, personalisation, and channel selection in real time, collapsing what used to require multi-step workflows.

Yet speed itself is emerging as a risk: agentic media buying operating without guardrails is already being linked to malware exposure and brand-safety failures. The decision for teams is no longer whether to adopt agents but how to build the oversight layer that keeps them from moving too fast.
ev: MarTech · When automation moves too fast

themes.head: AI Agents Become Your Brand's Second Audience
body: LLM-powered assistants and search agents are now crawling, summarising, and citing brand content independently of human queries. This creates a second audience — AI systems — whose interpretation of your website determines whether your brand is recommended or ignored in AI-generated answers.

Early movers are already optimising content structure and metadata for AI legibility, mirroring the early days of SEO. Partnerships like Getfluence & OtterlyAI are turning AI search-visibility scores into editorial action plans, signalling that AI-answer optimisation is becoming a discrete discipline inside content strategy.
ev: Fibr AI CEO on the second audience
MarTech · Brand measurement needs new truth

themes.head: The AI Readiness Gap Inside Enterprises
body: Large organisations are discovering that tooling is ahead of talent and governance. Not every marketer needs to be an AI builder, but every team needs someone who can translate AI capabilities into sound decisions — a role most enterprises have not yet defined or hired for.

The gap shows up concretely in data infrastructure: vendors like Seemoredata are selling Databricks cost-optimisation specifically so enterprises can free up budget to fund AI without adding net spend. The pattern — bolt-on optimisation to justify AI investment — suggests many organisations are still in a retrofitting phase rather than a transformation one.
ev: Typeface CRO on enterprise readiness gap
MarTech · Not everyone should be an AI builder

themes.head: AI-Native Creative & Content Pipelines Consolidate
body: The month's product moves reveal a clear direction: AI generation and professional editing tools are being stitched into single handoff workflows. Adobe's Claude Motion-to-Firefly connector, the Deepdub & Spikes multilingual content partnership, and OpenAI adding visuals to ChatGPT ads all point to end-to-end pipelines where humans review and approve rather than create from scratch.

Synthetic audience testing is emerging as the quality-control layer in these pipelines, letting teams pressure-test AI-generated campaigns against simulated segments before any real customer sees them. Together these moves suggest that within a planning cycle, the default creative workflow will be AI-first with human editorial oversight, not the reverse.
ev: Adobe Claude Motion to Firefly handoff

month.takeaway: Across every layer of the stack — budget, workflow, content, search, and talent — the real transformation is not adopting AI but building the judgment layer that keeps AI-speed decisions from outrunning human accountability.
